metadata.join_method: Exact ward_code and borough_code match to map geometry; no name matching or borough-value substitution.

periods.geography: December 2024 wards and local authority districts; matched by code to the GLA 2025 map layer
periods.population: Mid-2024; population change from mid-2023 to mid-2024

sources.note: December 2024 ward boundaries and LSOA 2021 to ward 2024 best-fit lookup.
Small-area population estimates, mid-2023 and mid-2024 (NM_2014_1).
Price Paid Data, category A standard market sales, calendar 2024 and 2025.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.note: English Indices of Deprivation 2025, File 7; population-weighted ward scores.
LSOA recorded offences over the latest 24 months in the bundled snapshot.
Common neighbourhood names for 2021 MSOAs; Open Parliament Licence.
Postcode to LSOA lookup built on the ONS Postcode Directory.

caveats: Whole LSOAs are assigned by best fit, so values near ward boundaries are approximate rather than exact official ward totals.
The 20 City of London wards without assigned LSOAs have geometry only. The five City wards with indicators have no Metropolitan Police crime figures; missing values remain null.
Recorded offences per 1,000 residents are affected by visitors and workers, particularly in central London; this is not a personal-risk measure.
Medians describe properties sold rather than a typical home. Fewer than 20 sales is flagged as unreliable; property-type medians can have still smaller samples.
Changes in sale medians reflect the mix of properties sold and do not measure investment returns. IoD 2025 is not comparable with IoD 2019.
Neighbourhood names overlap wards and are not separate mapped boundaries. Source periods differ and are labelled separately.
